seo_title: Cost of Living in Belgrade 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Belgrade per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A European city with a culture and language close to ours. One of the main IT hubs for Russian-speaking professionals: company registration, bank accounts and work residence permits — without aggressive bureaucracy.
pros: A large Russian-speaking community with its own infrastructure
An IT-friendly country with legal employment for remote workers
Close to Europe — Budapest is 6 hours away by train
cons: Smog and poor air quality in winter
Rents have risen 1.5 times over 2 years
Long-term visas turned out to be harder than expected

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: 30 days with a passport, stamped at the border.

visa_steps.title: White card
visa_steps.description: Registration of your place of residence with the police — mandatory within 24 hours.

visa_steps.title: Registering a sole proprietorship or company
visa_steps.description: Through a lawyer — 2–3 weeks, gaining PR-entrepreneur or DOO status.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Raiffeisen, OTP, Komercijalna — all work with Russians; you'll need company documents or a residence permit.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit
visa_steps.description: Through work, a company or family — submitted to the police at your place of residence, with review in 1–3 months.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Belgrade?
faq.answer: Serbian in Cyrillic, but many people in Belgrade speak Russian and English.

faq.question: Can I use a MIR card in Belgrade?
faq.answer: No, you need a local or a foreign non-MIR card.

faq.question: What is healthcare like in Belgrade?
faq.answer: Private care from 3,500 ₽ per appointment. Public care under insurance is available after getting a residence permit.

faq.question: How is the internet in Belgrade?
faq.answer: Good fibre across the city, plans run 1,500–2,500 ₽ a month.

faq.question: Is Belgrade safe?
faq.answer: Yes, crime is low and Serbs are friendly towards Russians.

faq.question: Can I work remotely without a residence permit in Belgrade?
faq.answer: Technically yes, but there are tax risks — it's better to set up a PR or DOO.

reviews.text: Serbs are open people and the language is quick to learn. The downside — local bureaucracy can take 2–3 months for a simple procedure.
I set up a company and got a residence permit through work. Prices are rising, but Belgrade is still cheaper than Prague and Berlin.
